chapters.title: David's Song of Deliverance
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 22

The LORD My Rock

1David spoke to the LORD the words of this song on the day the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.

2He said:
"The LORD is my rock, my fortress and my deliverer,

3my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge,
my shield and the horn of my salvation,
my stronghold and my refuge,
my savior; You save me from violence.

4I call on the LORD, who is worthy to be praised,
and I am saved from my enemies.

Out of Many Waters

5For the breakers of death surrounded me;
the torrents of worthlessness terrified me.

6The cords of Sheol were around me;
the snares of death confronted me.

7In my distress I called on the LORD;
to my God I called.
From His temple He heard my voice,
and my cry for help came into His ears.

8Then the earth shook and quaked;
the foundations of the heavens trembled
and shook, because He was angry.

9Smoke went up from His nostrils,
and devouring fire from His mouth;
coals blazed out from Him.

10He bent the heavens and came down,
with thick darkness under His feet.

11He rode on a cherub and flew;
He was seen on the wings of the wind.

12He made darkness a covering around Him,
a gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies.

13From the brightness before Him
coals of fire blazed out.

14The LORD thundered from the heavens;
the Most High uttered His voice.

15He sent out arrows and scattered them,
lightning, and routed them.

16The channels of the sea were seen;
the foundations of the world were laid bare
at the rebuke of the LORD,
at the blast of the breath of His nostrils.

17He reached from on high and took me;
He drew me out of many waters.

18He delivered me from my strong enemy,
from those who hated me,
for they were too mighty for me.

19They confronted me on the day of my calamity,
but the LORD was my support.

20He brought me out into a broad place;
He rescued me, because He delighted in me.

"With the Loyal You Show Yourself Loyal"

21The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness;
according to the cleanness of my hands He repaid me.

22For I have kept the ways of the LORD,
and have not wickedly departed from my God.

23For all His judgments were before me,
and from His statutes I did not turn aside.

24I was blameless before Him,
and I kept myself from my guilt.

25So the LORD repaid me according to my righteousness,
according to my cleanness in His sight.

26With the loyal You show Yourself loyal;
with the blameless man You show Yourself blameless.

27With the pure You show Yourself pure,
and with the crooked You show Yourself twisted.

28You save a humble people,
but Your eyes are on the haughty, to bring them down.

29For You are my lamp, O LORD;
the LORD lights up my darkness.

30For by You I can run against a troop;
by my God I can leap over a wall.

31This God — His way is blameless;
the word of the LORD is refined.
He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him.

32For who is God but the LORD?
Who is a rock but our God?

The God Who Trains My Hands

33This God is my strong fortress,
and He has set my way free and blameless.

34He makes my feet like the feet of a deer
and sets me on my high places.

35He trains my hands for war,
so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze.

36You have given me the shield of Your salvation,
and Your answering has made me great.

37You made room for my steps under me,
and my ankles did not give way.

38I pursued my enemies and destroyed them;
I did not turn back until they were consumed.

39I consumed them; I struck them through, so that they could not rise;
they fell under my feet.

40You girded me with strength for battle;
You made those who rose against me bow under me.

41You made my enemies turn their backs to me;
those who hated me I destroyed.

42They looked, but there was no one to save them;
to the LORD, but He did not answer them.

43I beat them fine as the dust of the earth;
I crushed them and stamped them down like the mud of the streets.

44You delivered me from the strife of my people;
You kept me as the head of nations.
A people I did not know serve me.

45Foreigners come cringing to me;
as soon as they hear, they obey me.

46Foreigners lose heart;
they gird themselves and come out of their strongholds.

"The LORD Lives"

47The LORD lives! Blessed be my rock,
and exalted be God, the rock of my salvation,

48the God who gives me vengeance
and brings down peoples under me,

49who brings me out from my enemies.
You exalt me above those who rise against me;
You deliver me from the man of violence.

50Therefore I will give thanks to You, O LORD, among the nations,
and sing praises to Your name.

51He is a tower of salvation for His king,
and shows loyal love to His anointed,
to David and to his seed forever."

Notes

  • v1 "the words of this song" — the song stands again as Psalm 18, with its own title, on the day the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul. The two copies differ in dozens of small places; the notes below give the ones that change the sense.

  • v5 "the breakers of death… the torrents of worthlessness" — mishberei mavet, the waves that break over a man. Psalm 18:4 has chevlei mavet, the cords of death, matching the cords of Sheol in the next line. Beliyya'al, worthlessness, the word used of Sheba and of Eli's sons (20:1; 1 Samuel 2:12), stands here beside death and Sheol.

  • v11 "He was seen on the wings of the wind" — va-yera. Psalm 18:10 has va-yede, He swooped, as in swooping as the eagle swoops (Deuteronomy 28:49). The two words differ in one letter, and the Greek has was seen, as here.

  • v12 "a gathering of waters" — chashrat mayim, a word found only here; Psalm 18:11 has cheshkhat mayim, darkness of waters, and the Greek agrees with the Psalm. The sense of chashrat is uncertain.

  • vv26–27 "With the loyal You show Yourself loyal… with the crooked You show Yourself twisted" — chasid, the one who keeps chesed, loyal love. Tittappal, from the root of petaltol, twisted, in a crooked and twisted generation (Deuteronomy 32:5).

  • v29 "For You are my lamp, O LORD" — ki attah niri. Psalm 18:28 has You light my lamp. The chapter before called David the lamp of Israel (21:17); here the LORD is his.

  • v33 "He has set my way free and blameless" — va-yatter tamim darki, from natar, to let loose. Psalm 18:32 has va-yitten, and He made my way blameless; the Greek has shook out. The written text has darko, His way; the text follows the read form, darki, my way.

speech.text: 2 Samuel 22
The LORD My Rock
David spoke to the LORD the words of this song on the day the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
He said: "The LORD is my rock, my fortress and my deliverer,
my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold and my refuge, my savior; You save me from violence.
I call on the LORD, who is worthy to be praised, and I am saved from my enemies.
Out of Many Waters
For the breakers of death surrounded me; the torrents of worthlessness terrified me.
The cords of Sheol were around me; the snares of death confronted me.
In my distress I called on the LORD; to my God I called. From His temple He heard my voice, and my cry for help came into His ears.
Then the earth shook and quaked; the foundations of the heavens trembled and shook, because He was angry.
Smoke went up from His nostrils, and devouring fire from His mouth; coals blazed out from Him.
He bent the heavens and came down, with thick darkness under His feet.
He rode on a cherub and flew; He was seen on the wings of the wind.
He made darkness a covering around Him, a gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies.
From the brightness before Him coals of fire blazed out.
The LORD thundered from the heavens; the Most High uttered His voice.
He sent out arrows and scattered them, lightning, and routed them.
The channels of the sea were seen; the foundations of the world were laid bare at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of His nostrils.
He reached from on high and took me; He drew me out of many waters.
He delivered me from my strong enemy, from those who hated me, for they were too mighty for me.
They confronted me on the day of my calamity, but the LORD was my support.
He brought me out into a broad place; He rescued me, because He delighted in me.
"With the Loyal You Show Yourself Loyal"
The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands He repaid me.
For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and have not wickedly departed from my God.
For all His judgments were before me, and from His statutes I did not turn aside.
I was blameless before Him, and I kept myself from my guilt.
So the LORD repaid me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness in His sight.
With the loyal You show Yourself loyal; with the blameless man You show Yourself blameless.
With the pure You show Yourself pure, and with the crooked You show Yourself twisted.
You save a humble people, but Your eyes are on the haughty, to bring them down.
For You are my lamp, O LORD; the LORD lights up my darkness.
For by You I can run against a troop; by my God I can leap over a wall.
This God — His way is blameless; the word of the LORD is refined. He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him.
For who is God but the LORD? Who is a rock but our God?
The God Who Trains My Hands
This God is my strong fortress, and He has set my way free and blameless.
He makes my feet like the feet of a deer and sets me on my high places.
He trains my hands for war, so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
You have given me the shield of Your salvation, and Your answering has made me great.
You made room for my steps under me, and my ankles did not give way.
I pursued my enemies and destroyed them; I did not turn back until they were consumed.
I consumed them; I struck them through, so that they could not rise; they fell under my feet.
You girded me with strength for battle; You made those who rose against me bow under me.
You made my enemies turn their backs to me; those who hated me I destroyed.
They looked, but there was no one to save them; to the LORD, but He did not answer them.
I beat them fine as the dust of the earth; I crushed them and stamped them down like the mud of the streets.
You delivered me from the strife of my people; You kept me as the head of nations. A people I did not know serve me.
Foreigners come cringing to me; as soon as they hear, they obey me.
Foreigners lose heart; they gird themselves and come out of their strongholds.
"The LORD Lives"
The LORD lives! Blessed be my rock, and exalted be God, the rock of my salvation,
the God who gives me vengeance and brings down peoples under me,
who brings me out from my enemies. You exalt me above those who rise against me; You deliver me from the man of violence.
Therefore I will give thanks to You, O LORD, among the nations, and sing praises to Your name.
He is a tower of salvation for His king, and shows loyal love to His anointed, to David and to his seed forever."

chapters.title: David's Last Words and His Mighty Men
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 23

The Last Words of David

1These are the last words of David:
"The word of David son of Jesse,
the word of the man who was raised on high,
the anointed of the God of Jacob,
the sweet singer of Israel:

2The Spirit of the LORD spoke by me;
His word was on my tongue.

3The God of Israel said,
the Rock of Israel spoke to me:
'One who rules over men in righteousness,
who rules in the fear of God,

4is like the light of morning when the sun rises,
a morning without clouds,
like the grass from the earth
after the brightness of rain.'

5Is not my house so with God?
For He has made with me an everlasting covenant,
ordered in all things and secured.
Will He not make all my salvation
and all my desire to grow?

6But the worthless are all like thorns thrust away,
for they cannot be taken with the hand;

7the man who touches them
arms himself with iron and the shaft of a spear,
and they are utterly burned with fire where they lie."

The Three

8These are the names of David's mighty men: Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite, chief of the Three. He was Adino the Eznite; he drew his sword against eight hundred, whom he killed at one time.

9After him was Eleazar son of Dodo, son of Ahohi, one of the three mighty men with David when they taunted the Philistines who were gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel withdrew.

10He got up and struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary and his hand clung to the sword. The LORD brought about a great victory that day, and the people returned after him only to strip the dead.

11After him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines gathered at Lehi, where there was a plot of ground full of lentils, and the people fled from the Philistines.

12But he took his stand in the middle of the plot, defended it and struck down the Philistines, and the LORD brought about a great victory.

Water from the Well of Bethlehem

13Three of the thirty chiefs went down at harvest time and came to David at the cave of Adullam, while a troop of Philistines was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.

14David was then in the stronghold, and the Philistine garrison was then at Bethlehem.

15David longed and said, "If only someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate!"

16So the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines, drew water from the well of Bethlehem that was by the gate, and carried it and brought it to David. But he would not drink it; he poured it out to the LORD.

17He said, "Far be it from me, O LORD, that I should do this. Is it not the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?" So he would not drink it. These things the three mighty men did.

Abishai and Benaiah

18Abishai, the brother of Joab, son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Three. He wielded his spear against three hundred, whom he killed, and won a name among the Three.

19Was he not the most honored of the Three? He became their commander, but he did not attain to the Three.

20Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the son of a man of valor from Kabzeel, great in deeds. He struck down the two Ariels of Moab. He also went down and struck down a lion inside a pit on a day of snow.

21He struck down an Egyptian, a man of great stature. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand, but Benaiah went down to him with a staff, snatched the spear out of the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear.

22These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did, and he won a name among the three mighty men.

23He was honored among the Thirty, but he did not attain to the Three. David set him over his bodyguard.

The Thirty

24Asahel the brother of Joab was among the Thirty; Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem;

25Shammah the Harodite; Elika the Harodite;

26Helez the Paltite; Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite;

27Abiezer the Anathothite; Mebunnai the Hushathite;

28Zalmon the Ahohite; Maharai the Netophathite;

29Heleb son of Baanah the Netophathite; Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the sons of Benjamin;

30Benaiah a Pirathonite; Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash;

31Abi-albon the Arbathite; Azmaveth the Barhumite;

32Eliahba the Shaalbonite; the sons of Jashen, Jonathan;

33Shammah the Hararite; Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite;

34Eliphelet son of Ahasbai, son of the Maacathite; Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite;

35Hezrai the Carmelite; Paarai the Arbite;

36Igal son of Nathan of Zobah; Bani the Gadite;

37Zelek the Ammonite; Naharai the Beerothite, armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah;

38Ira the Ithrite; Gareb the Ithrite;

39Uriah the Hittite: thirty-seven in all.

Notes

  • v1 "The word of David son of Jesse, the word of the man who was raised on high" — ne'um, the word for a speech given by God, used in the oracles of Balaam, the word of the man whose eye is opened (Numbers 24:3). The sweet singer of Israel: ne'im zemirot Yisra'el, which can also be read the favorite of the songs of Israel.

  • v2 "The Spirit of the LORD spoke by me" — the Spirit that rushed on David from that day forward when Samuel anointed him (1 Samuel 16:13).

  • vv4–5 "like the light of morning… an everlasting covenant" — berit olam, the promise Nathan brought: Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever (7:16).

  • vv6–7 "the worthless are all like thorns" — beliyya'al, the word of Sheba (20:1) and of the torrents of death in the song before (22:5). No one takes thorns in the hand; they are handled with iron and burned.

  • v8 "He was Adino the Eznite; he drew his sword against eight hundred" — the Hebrew has hu Adino ha-Etsni al shemoneh me'ot chalal, he was Adino the Eznite, against eight hundred slain, with no verb. The Greek has he drew his sword against eight hundred. Chronicles names the man Jashobeam son of Hachmoni and has he wielded his spear against three hundred slain at one time (1 Chronicles 11:11), the words used of Abishai in v18. The text follows the Greek and keeps the Hebrew number.

  • v10 "his hand clung to the sword" — va-tidbaq yado el ha-cherev: he fought until he could not open his hand. The LORD brought about a great victory, teshu'ah, is said of Eleazar and of Shammah (v12).

  • v11 "a plot of ground full of lentils" — Chronicles tells this stand under Eleazar's name and has full of barley (1 Chronicles 11:13–14).

  • vv16–17 "he poured it out to the LORD… Is it not the blood of the men" — the water was bought with the lives of three men, and David treats it as blood, which is not to be taken but poured out: Only the blood you shall not eat; pour it out on the ground like water (Deuteronomy 12:16).

  • v20 "the two Ariels of Moab… a lion inside a pit on a day of snow" — shenei ari'el Mo'av. What an ari'el is here is not known: the Greek has the two sons of Ariel, making it a name. The word is built from ari, lion, and a lion follows in the same verse.

  • vv34, 39 "Eliam son of Ahithophel… Uriah the Hittite: thirty-seven in all" — the list closes with Uriah, whom David had killed (11:15–17). The names in vv24–39 number thirty-one, or thirty-two if the sons of Jashen counts as one; with the Three, Abishai and Benaiah they make thirty-six or thirty-seven.

chapters.title: David's Census
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 24

The Census

1Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He incited David against them, saying, "Go, number Israel and Judah."

2So the king said to Joab, the commander of the army, who was with him, "Go through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and count the people, so that I may know the number of the people."

3But Joab said to the king, "May the LORD your God add to the people a hundred times as many as they are, while the eyes of my lord the king still see it. But why does my lord the king delight in this thing?"

4But the king's word prevailed against Joab and the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army went out from the king's presence to count the people of Israel.

5They crossed the Jordan and camped in Aroer, south of the city that is in the middle of the valley of Gad, and toward Jazer.

6Then they came to Gilead and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi, and they came to Dan-jaan and around to Sidon.

7They came to the fortress of Tyre and to all the cities of the Hivites and the Canaanites, and they went out to the Negev of Judah at Beersheba.

8When they had gone through all the land, they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.

9Joab gave the king the number of the people counted: in Israel there were eight hundred thousand valiant men who drew the sword, and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand.

The Three Choices

10But David's heart struck him after he had numbered the people. David said to the LORD, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done. But now, O LORD, please take away the guilt of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."

11When David got up in the morning, the word of the LORD had come to Gad the prophet, David's seer, saying,

12"Go and say to David, 'Thus says the LORD: I am laying three things before you. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you.'"

13So Gad came to David and told him, and said to him, "Shall three years of famine come to you in your land? Or will you flee three months before your enemies while they pursue you? Or shall there be three days of plague in your land? Now consider and decide what answer I shall return to the one who sent me."

14David said to Gad, "I am in great distress. Let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are great; but let me not fall into the hand of man."

The Plague

15So the LORD sent a plague on Israel from the morning until the appointed time, and seventy thousand men of the people died, from Dan to Beersheba.

16When the messenger stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD relented from the evil and said to the messenger who was destroying the people, "Enough! Now hold back your hand." The messenger of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

17When David saw the messenger who was striking the people, he spoke to the LORD and said, "It is I who have sinned, and I who have done wrong. But these sheep, what have they done? Please let Your hand be against me and against my father's house."

The Threshing Floor of Araunah

18Gad came to David that day and said to him, "Go up, raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."

19So David went up at Gad's word, as the LORD had commanded.

20When Araunah looked down and saw the king and his servants coming over toward him, Araunah went out and paid homage to the king with his face to the ground.

21Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" David said, "To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to the LORD, so that the plague may be held back from the people."

22Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take it and offer up what is good in his eyes. Here are the oxen for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and the yokes of the oxen for the wood.

23All this, O king, Araunah gives to the king." Araunah also said to the king, "May the LORD your God accept you."

24But the king said to Araunah, "No, but I will surely buy it from you for a price. I will not offer burnt offerings to the LORD my God that cost me nothing." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

25David built an altar to the LORD there and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. So the LORD heeded prayers for the land, and the plague was held back from Israel.

Notes

  • v1 "Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He incited David against them" — va-yasset, incited. Again looks back to the famine of 21:1. Chronicles tells the same story with another subject: Satan stood up against Israel and incited David to number Israel (1 Chronicles 21:1). The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • vv2–3 "count the people… why does my lord the king delight in this thing?" — the text does not say what was wrong in the count. The law of the census warns that each man must give a ransom for his life to the LORD when they are numbered — so there will be no plague among them (Exodus 30:12), and a plague follows here.

  • v9 "eight hundred thousand… five hundred thousand" — Chronicles has a million one hundred thousand for Israel and four hundred seventy thousand for Judah (1 Chronicles 21:5). The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v10 "David's heart struck him" — va-yakh lev David oto, as when he cut off the edge of Saul's robe (1 Samuel 24:5). I have acted very foolishly, niskalti, the word Samuel used of Saul (1 Samuel 13:13).

  • v13 "three years of famine" — the Hebrew has seven years. The Greek has three years, and so does Chronicles (1 Chronicles 21:12); the three choices are three years, three months and three days (v12, three things). The text follows the Greek and Chronicles.

  • v15 "until the appointed time" — ad et mo'ed; the Greek has until the hour of the midday meal, and adds that David chose the plague in the days of wheat harvest. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • vv16–17 "the LORD relented from the evil… these sheep, what have they done?" — va-yinnachem YHWH el ha-ra'ah. The shepherd king offers himself and his father's house in place of the flock.

  • vv16, 18 "Araunah the Jebusite" — the written forms vary, ha-Awarnah (v16) and Araniah (v18); the text follows the read form, Aravnah, throughout. Chronicles calls him Ornan (1 Chronicles 21:15).

  • v24 "that cost me nothing… fifty shekels of silver" — chinnam, for nothing. Chronicles has six hundred shekels of gold by weight (1 Chronicles 21:25). The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v25 "the LORD heeded prayers for the land" — the words of 21:14. The Greek adds that Solomon later enlarged this altar. Chronicles names the place: Solomon built the house of the LORD on Mount Moriah… on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite (2 Chronicles 3:1), the name of the land where Abraham was sent with Isaac (Genesis 22:2).
